questions.q: What does LEFT JOIN guarantee compared to INNER JOIN?
options: Every row from the left table appears in the results, matched or not
Every row from the right table appears, matched or not
Rows are sorted automatically by the join column
Only rows matching on both sides appear, just like INNER JOIN
questions.explain: LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the table named in FROM, regardless of whether a match exists on the right.

questions.q: What value appears in the right table's columns when a LEFT JOIN finds no match?
options: NULL
An empty string
Zero
The query fails with an error
questions.explain: Unmatched right-side columns are filled with NULL, exactly like a missing value from Lesson 16.

questions.q: What determines which table is the 'left' table in a JOIN?
options: Whichever table's primary key comes first alphabetically
The table that was created first in the database
Whichever table has more rows
The table named in the FROM clause, written first in the query
questions.explain: 'Left' and 'right' refer purely to position in the query text — FROM names the left table, JOIN names the right.

questions.q: How do you use LEFT JOIN to find rows with no match at all?
options: LEFT JOIN cannot be used to find unmatched rows
Add an ORDER BY on the unmatched column
Add WHERE on a right-table column IS NULL, since that column can only be NULL if the match failed
Switch to INNER JOIN instead
questions.explain: WHERE sod.ProductID IS NULL isolates exactly the rows where the LEFT JOIN found nothing on the right side.

questions.q: In a query finding products that have never sold, why check sod.ProductID IS NULL specifically?
options: It filters out products with a NULL name
sod.ProductID can only be NULL if no matching SalesOrderDetail row was found for that product
It's an arbitrary choice — any column from either table would work identically
ProductID is always NULL by default in SalesOrderDetail
questions.explain: Since ProductID is a foreign key (Lesson 21) that would normally always have a value, its NULL here specifically signals 'no match found.'
